{"documentId": "f_dc45e0e5a8b8635c1b82b2", "title": "Beta message rule", "name": "Beta message rule", "revisionId": "740e0d0bac", "createdTime": "2025-09-26T17:10:54Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-26T17:10:54Z", "text": "Beta message rule
A message is anything the game puts on a player's phone while the game is closed.
Run these tests in order and stop at the first one that fails.
1. The feature behind it is in the beta.
2. The client can send it without a server.
3. The client already schedules it.
4. It can reach the players it is written for. A player only counts once our own permission ask has happened, the settings toggle doesn't count. It fails only if none of them count.
5. It fires on the right day. The hour doesn't matter for beta, the day does.
6. Vincent has seen it arrive on both iOS and Android.
Go: it passes all six. Drop: it fails test 1, or the client already covers it under another message, then name that message. Hold: anything else, and name the test it failed.
In the beta means live in Zombie Match today or on the BETA list of the ZM ROADMAP board.
Neither status column on the sheet decides anything.
What Vincent counts as seen is in his QA note. The permission ask is Robert's call.
The final headline is the latest line I've called. A line that differs from what the client ships needs a string ticket under DES-314, because the strings are hard-coded, so open one when you make the call. Emoji don't count as a different line. Final headline and String change are only for Go rows. Audience is who the ask says it's for.
Drop tickets go to Canceled, Go tickets stay as they are, Hold tickets go back to Todo unless the roadmap says otherwise.
"}

## 🧩 **Endless Mode – Engineering Summary**

### 🔧 Initial Setup

- Game starts with **40–45 sets** (a set = 3 items).
- **8 unique item types**, with size distribution:
  - 2 Large, 4 medium, 2 Small.
- Entire **item pool is defined by the designer** for each endless variant.
- Monsters also follow **30-second "tracks"**, authored by designers using level editor tools.

---

### 🔄 Refill System (Every 30 seconds)

1. **Track matched items** from the last 30 seconds.
2. **Refill those exact items** to keep total set count at 40–45.
3. Each refill is simulated and checked against a **growing Unique Item Cap**:

Refill #Time (s)Unique Cap130826093909412010.........1236014

---

### 🧠 Refill Logic Rules

1. **Simulate a refill**: Replace all matched items 1:1.
2. **Count unique items** on the new board.
3. If unique count is **below cap**:
   - Attempt to **substitute refilled items** with new unique items one-by-one.
   - After each substitution, re-check unique count.
4. If still short:
   - Remove a **fraction of total sets** = `#missingUniques / targetUniqueCap`.
   - Replace them with random sets using new unique items to reach the cap.

**Key principle:** Total number of sets never changes; only uniqueness does.

---

### 💥 New Mechanic: The Nuke (Replaces Boss Buster)

- **Builds power** by matching items:
  `NukePower += itemAttackPower × 10% × comboMultiplier`
- **Combo System**:
  - Starts at **1x**.
  - Combo meter fills after each match and **decays** over time.
  - If matched before timeout, combo increases.
  - Decay window shrinks by 0.25s each level (starts at 4.5s).
  - Max achievable combo: 18x.
  - The **next match** receives the combo multiplier shown.

ComboTimeout2x4.5s3x4.25s......18x~0s

- **Minimum power to activate Nuke** = 50.

The game starts out fairly easy, and players who excel at match 3 games can easily defeat any monsters through good puzzle play. However as players approach mid and late game, the difficulty of the game doesn't really revolve around the matches. ", "channel": "C0880U9751A", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1743616941.002449"}, {"ts": "1743616638.279219", "type": "message", "text": ":boom: *Direct-to-Boss Naming Ideas*
:gun: Tactical & Descriptive
• *Boss Seekers*
•  → Like heat-seeking missiles — they _find_ and _hit_ the boss.
• *Boss Shots*
•  → Super clear, simple, and casual. Easy to use in a tutorial.
• *Direct Hits*
•  → Communicates the straight-to-boss behavior clearly.
• *Boss Piercers*
•  → A little more edgy — implies they punch _through_ the horde.
• *Bossline Items*
•  → Play on “frontline” or “backline” — these go straight to the bossline.
:dart: More Flavorful / Thematic
• *Sniper Matches*
•  → Clean, accurate, and implies long-range precision.
• *H[USERNAME_49260]*
•  → Gamers get it instantly — feels powerful and direct.
• *VIP Hits* _(or Target Hits)_
•  → “Very Important Punch” to the boss. A little cheeky.
• *Backdoor Blasters*
•  → Fun, game-y, and implies sneaky boss access.
• *Skip Shots*
•  → Implies skipping the line straight to the end target.
:brain: Smart & Player-Friendly
• *Boss Trackers*
•  → Makes it sound like these items “know” where to aim.
• *Bypass Shots* _(repackaged internal term)_
•  → If you like the clarity of “bypass,” just attach a more dynamic word to it.
• *Boss Beelines*
•  → A play on “making a beeline for something” – direct path.

• Cooking games, where you are upgrading ingredients, cookware and even customers. These RPG modifications often change the scoring mechanic or provide players with an advantage with increased in efficiency in scoring output.
• Idle games. Adventure Capitalist. The whole point of the game is to spend money, upgrade "thin[USERNAME_6903]" just to.... earn more money _faster_ so you can... spend more money... to upgrade more "things"
• Clicker games. Tap Titan. The game literally involves click anywhere on the screen to attack a single "monster" on screen. Killing monster spawns another one immediately after, however player is awarded in the process. The monsters get stronger and stronger with more and more HP. Players obtain items and permanent upgrades that allows higher damage output, and even auto clicking......... Damage goes from 10s, 100s, 1000s and eventually a simple 10 to the power of X function.
• Puzzle match 3s. Empires and Puzzles. The game starts out fairly easy, and players who excel at match 3 games can easily defeat any monsters through good puzzle play. However as players approach mid and late game, the difficulty of the game doesn't really revolve around the matches. One can be the best match 3 player and still lose simply because their 4x base isn't upgraded enough, nor is their collection of characters.
• MOBA style RPGs, We are warriors - You have a base, enemy has a base, both bases spawn attacking Units and send them at the opposing base. Player has very little input other than when to spawn what unit, but have no actual micro controls of the Units. Units auto march and auto engage any enemy until the enemy base is destroyed. The upgrades follow a well optimized math formula, and the Units and modifications are be interesting to players.
• Horde Survivor games, <http://survivor.IO|survivor.IO> - Open map kill infinite monster games. Roguelike, self explanatory.
• Dungeon Crawling RPGs, [USERNAME_14652] - self explanatory.
• Tower defense style survival RPGs, BangBang Survivor - A stream of monsters come at your fortress, defeat monsters before they destroy you. Our top half of the game the "stage" mimics this. Game features both roguelike and permanent upgrades via pets/gears/runes/characters/others
• Probably many others I have missed", "channel": "C0880U9751A", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1737095530.810589"}, {"ts": "1686280147.933529", "type": "message", "text": "if we give players an opportunity to horde something they will horde it :slightly_smiling_face:", "channel": "C04S28HSD0U", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID"}, {"ts": "1686279892.113399", "type": "message", "text": "Just trying to think if There was an inventory system for time duration boosts, I don't think you can "horde" them", "channel": "C04S28HSD0U", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID"}], "has_more": false, "total_count": 33, "response_metadata": {"next_cursor": ""}}

input.title: String change: Lapsed 7 days headline to "Your Squad Is Waiting"
input.description:
The Lapsed 7 days message (DES-317) is a Go for beta. Leonard's latest headline call is "Your Squad Is Waiting" (from the Sep 30 lapsed copy check, which replaces "Your Squad Needs You Back" from the art thread). The body stays the same.

The client still ships the old headline, hard-coded in NotificationManager.cs (`WeeklyReminderTitle = "They've Taken Over… Can You Stop Them? 😱"`).

To do:
- Change `WeeklyReminderTitle` to "Your Squad Is Waiting". The body is unchanged. Keeping or dropping the emoji is fine either way.
- Note that this string goes out on day 7, 14, 21 and 28 (BatchScheduleWeeklyNotifications repeats it for 4 weeks).
- Vincent re-checks it on store builds on both iOS and Android once it ships.

input.title: ZM Beta Player Messages - Team Note (Oct 1 2025)
input.bodyText:
ZM Beta Player Messages: what we actually say to players

Sources: PNs Beta tab, DES-314 asks plus DES-313, Beta message rule, NotificationManager.cs on main, backend schedules, and Vincent's Phone message checks plus his later corrections. The full call list is in the "ZM Beta Player Messages - Calls" sheet in the same folder.

1) Retention: Sep 15 cohort week (warehouse, USER_COHORT_RETENTION)
- iOS: 237 installs. D1 31.65%, D7 9.28%
- Android: 103 installs. D1 37.86%, D7 10.68%

2) Lapsed reminders the client schedules, day by day
These are scheduled locally when the app goes to background. They only go out once our own permission ask has run (after level 20) or the player has switched notifications on in settings.
- Day 1: "The Horde Is Growing… 🧟‍♂️" (Lapsed 1 day). Go.
- Day 7: "They've Taken Over… Can You Stop Them? 😱" (Lapsed 7 days). Go. The headline changes to "Your Squad Is Waiting" (DES-346).
- Day 14, Day 21 and Day 28: the same 7-day message again. The weekly batch repeats for 4 weeks, which is why the Lapsed 14 days ask is a Drop.
- Nothing on day 2-6, nothing between the weekly repeats, and nothing after day 28. That means day 3 (DES-342) and day 30 (DES-343) are Holds: not scheduled yet.

3) Already scheduled by the client but still a Hold, and why
- Lives recharged ("Full Ammo Reloaded!", DES-315). Test 6: it isn't seen on both platforms. On Sep 30 it didn't arrive on the iOS 0.3.49 store build after a full refill, tried twice, and Vincent took his tick off.
- Finish first mission (DES-318). Test 4: it can't reach its audience. It is only scheduled for players below level 20, but our permission ask runs after level 20, so nobody it's written for has had our ask. The settings toggle doesn't count.
- Plague Race (DES-319). Test 6: not seen on iOS. Vincent's iOS tick was on the 5-minute-timer build, and the real iOS 0.3.40 store build never showed it. Android is fine. The daily timing is fine because there's always a race on.
- Weekly Leaderboard reset (DES-320). Test 5: it fires on the wrong day. The client schedules it 7, 14, 21 and 28 days after the last session, but leagues reset Mondays 00:00 UTC. It only lands on reset day if the player last played on a Monday.

4) Counts
32 messages in total: 14 PNs Beta rows (Win & Collect is DES-313) plus 18 asks. Go 2, Hold 24, Drop 6.
- Go: Lapsed 1 day and Lapsed 7 days. Both are on the Push Notifications card checklist for Vincent.
- Drop: Hourly Coins, Treasure Hunt, Streak Fever and Axe Arena (none of them is in the beta), Comeback gift (a v2 idea), and Lapsed 14 days (already covered by Lapsed 7 days).
- Hold tickets go to Backlog, unassigned, per the BETA "Fix TECH ISSUES" card. Most Holds just need a local timer added in NotificationManager (test 3). Five need a server send (test 2): Endless weekly result, Season Pass premium nudge, Plague Race result, Support reply waiting, New levels added.

Note: neither status column on the PN sheet decided anything here. The sheet marks six rows Ready, and only the two lapsed ones pass all six tests.

content.text:
I've done everything in Leonard's DM and sent him the counts there. Out of 32 messages (the 14 rows on the PNs Beta tab plus 18 asks people filed), **2 are Go, 24 are Hold and 6 are Drop**.

**Go**
- **Lapsed 1 day** ("The Horde Is Growing… 🧟‍♂️"). No wording change needed.
- **Lapsed 7 days.** Leonard's latest line, from his Sep 30 "Lapsed copy check" calendar event, is "Your Squad Is Waiting". The game still has the old headline built in, so I opened DES-346 (assigned to you, Todo) to change the text.

**Drop**
- Hourly Coins, Treasure Hunt, Streak Fever and Axe Arena: none of these features is in the beta.
- Comeback gift: Leonard already called it a version 2 idea.
- Lapsed 14 days: the game already repeats the 7-day message on day 14, 21 and 28, so it's covered.

**The sheet said six were Ready, but only the two lapsed ones pass.** The other four are Holds:
- **Full Ammo (lives recharged):** Vincent took back his iOS sign-off on Sep 30 because it didn't arrive on iOS 0.3.49.
- **Plague Race:** his iOS check was on a test build with shortened timers, and it never showed on the real store build.
- **Finish first mission:** it only goes to players below level 20, and nobody there has had our permission ask yet (it runs after level 20).
- **Weekly Leaderboard:** it fires 7 days after the player's last session, not on the Monday reset.

**Retention, Sep 15 install week (warehouse)**

| Platform | Installs | D1 | D7 |
|---|---|---|---|
| iOS | 237 | 31.65% | 9.28% |
| Android | 103 | 37.86% | 10.68% |

**What I changed**
- **Your Drive folder:** the sheet "ZM Beta Player Messages - Calls (Oct 1 2025)" and the one-page note "ZM Beta Player Messages - Team Note (Oct 1 2025)".
- **Tickets:** every ticket has its call as a comment.
  - The 6 Drops are Canceled.
  - The two Go tickets stay Done.
  - The 24 Holds went to Backlog and I removed the assignee. The rule doc says Holds go back to Todo unless the roadmap says otherwise. The roadmap's BETA list says held tickets sit in Backlog, unassigned, until the beta build is out, so I followed that.
- **No duplicate ticket:** the sheet's Win & Collect row is the same message Calvin already filed as DES-313, so that one ticket covers both.
- **Trello:** the push notifications card has a checklist with the two Go messages for Vincent.
- **Emails:** Brian, Robert, Oliver, Julia, Owen, Calvin and Martin each got one covering their asks. Calvin's also tells him he's no longer assigned to DES-313.

**Judgement calls Leonard may want to check**
- I counted Lapsed 30 days as a Hold, not a Drop. The last reminder the game sends is on day 28, which isn't day 30.
- I counted Free shop coins as a Hold, separate from the dropped Hourly Coins. Free shop coins are live in the shop; Hourly Coins isn't in the beta.
